statement: For every m>0, T_b>0, gamma>0 and spatially homogeneous velocity Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with force F(t), initialized at its Maxwellian equilibrium and differentiated at F=0, the current response kernel is chi_gamma(t)=1_{t>=0} exp(-gamma t)/m. Its causal resolvent is chi_tilde_gamma(z)=1/[m(z+gamma)] for Re(z)>0. The equilibrium velocity covariance is C_gamma(t)=(k_B T_b/m)exp(-gamma t) for t>=0, so chi_gamma(t)=beta C_gamma(t) exactly.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: m,T_b,gamma are fixed positive real numbers for each member of the family.
beta=(k_B T_b)^(-1), sigma^2=(beta m)^(-1), M is the centered Gaussian with variance sigma^2.
f is normalized; integrations by parts have vanishing velocity-boundary terms.
The observable is mean velocity and the input is force, with force entering the acceleration as F/m.
The response means the derivative at zero applied force, at fixed gamma; position and nonuniform spatial modes are outside the stated model.
proof_pointer: RESULT.txt, sections 'Linear response and resolvent' and 'Fluctuation–dissipation identity and proof'. The first Hermite mode vM is invariant, L(vM)=-gamma vM; the OU SDE gives the covariance directly.

supplied_vs_acquired.note: This is an analytic model calculation, not an empirically fitted response.

costs.analytic_arithmetic: O(1) scalar operations after the parameters are supplied
costs.precision: For chi(0)=1/(m gamma), relative parameter errors propagate at first order as |Delta chi|/|chi| <= |Delta m|/m + |Delta gamma|/gamma. An absolute gamma error |Delta gamma| <= epsilon*m*gamma^2 suffices locally for absolute response error epsilon.
costs.trajectory_acquisition_if_empirical: A time horizon gamma^(-1) log(1/epsilon) is needed to observe decay to relative level epsilon; sample-count cost is not derived.

equal_input_baseline.direct_kinetic_method: Solve the linearized PDE; chi(t)=exp(-gamma t)/m and step response at T is (1-exp(-gamma T))/(m gamma).
equal_input_baseline.equilibrium_fluctuation_method: Compute C(t)=(k_B T_b/m)exp(-gamma t); beta*C(t) and beta*integral_0^T C(s) ds reproduce the same impulse and step responses.
equal_input_baseline.outcome: Exact algebraic agreement for every admitted parameter and finite horizon; this is an internal matched calculation, not external validation.

falsifier: For any m,T_b,gamma>0, a disagreement between the direct first-order PDE solution and beta times the equilibrium velocity covariance under the same conventions falsifies the identity.

primary_sources.role: kinetic Brownian equation and force setting
primary_sources.citation: H. A. Kramers, Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions, Physica 7(4), 284-304 (April 1940).
primary_sources.access_note: Publisher DOI page was inaccessible in this check; metadata was cross-checked at https://cir.nii.ac.jp/crid/1360855568683783168. No equation-level source attribution is made.

primary_sources.citation: R. Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes. I. General Theory and Simple Applications to Magnetic and Conduction Problems, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12(6), 570-586 (June 1957).
primary_sources.access_note: The journal abstract states that complex susceptibilities/conductivities are expressed in terms of time fluctuations. A 17-page mirror was opened, but equation text was not extracted; the special-case proof is provided here directly.

unresolved: No claim for non-reversible dynamics, non-equilibrium steady states, or nonuniform spatial modes.
No empirical validation or general new result is claimed.

statement: At fixed m>0 and T_b>0, the homogeneous OU kinetic family has exact mean-zero spectral gap gamma and static current susceptibility chi_tilde_gamma(0)=1/(m gamma). Hence the zero-frequency response is not uniformly bounded over gamma>0 as the gap closes, although for each fixed gamma>0 the response kernel decays exponentially and every fixed-time step response is finite. This one-mode example is sharp because source and observable both occupy the slow first Hermite mode.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: Fix m,T_b>0 and let gamma range over all positive values.
Static susceptibility is the derivative of stationary mean velocity with respect to constant force, equivalently the zero-frequency causal response integral.
Finite-time response is evaluated at a fixed horizon independent of gamma. No uniform-in-gamma exponential-decay claim is made.
proof_pointer: RESULT.txt, sections 'Linear response and resolvent' and 'Gap-closing conclusion and sharpness'. For fixed T_f, |delta j(T_f)| <= |F_0|T_f/m, while chi_tilde_gamma(0)=1/(m gamma) diverges.

costs.model_size: One exact invariant Hermite mode; O(1) analytic expression.
costs.finite_time_acquisition: For empirical resolution of an epsilon-relative decay, the observation horizon scales at least gamma^(-1)log(1/epsilon).
costs.precision: Absolute precision for the parameter gamma must scale as epsilon*m*gamma^2 to guarantee absolute error epsilon in 1/(m gamma), locally.

equal_input_baseline: Direct current response and the equilibrium Green-Kubo/FDT integral use identical m,T_b,gamma and give exactly 1/(m gamma). At m=k_B T_b=F_0=T_f=1, gamma=1,0.1,0.01 give finite-horizon step responses approximately 0.6321206,0.9516258,0.9950166 and static values 1,10,100.
falsifier: The explicit resolvent formula would have to fail for some gamma>0, or a claimed gamma-uniform finite bound would have to coexist with 1/(m gamma) for arbitrarily small positive gamma.
scientific_boundary: This refutes a general inference from pointwise relaxation/finite-time boundedness to uniform dc control. It does not imply divergence for every gap-closing kinetic model; vanishing slow-mode overlap can change the outcome.
unresolved: Whether a specific non-OU kinetic model has nonvanishing overlap with its slow modes requires separate analysis.

statement: For a reversible equilibrium generator L with discrete mean-zero spectral expansion L psi_k=-lambda_k psi_k, lambda_k>0, and a matched force-response source/observable A for which the FDT pairing holds and the inverse-generator quadratic form is finite, the zero-frequency response is beta*sum_k |<A,psi_k>|^2/lambda_k. A positive gap lower bound gives a norm-over-gap bound; closing gaps alone give no uniform bound unless the overlap weights on slow modes also suppress the inverse rates.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: L is self-adjoint and nonpositive on the mean-zero equilibrium Hilbert space.
The perturbation is conjugate to A so the response kernel is beta*<A,exp(tL)A>.
The spectral sum is interpreted by the spectral theorem and is finite for each model under consideration.
proof_pointer: Expand A in the orthonormal eigenbasis and integrate beta*sum_k |<A,psi_k>|^2 exp(-lambda_k t) termwise when the nonnegative integral is finite; monotone convergence gives the stated sum.

costs.information: Requires the equilibrium generator, observable/source overlap, and spectral measure; these are supplied in the conditional statement.
costs.precision: A finite truncation needs control of the omitted low-rate spectral mass; no uniform truncation algorithm or cost is claimed.

falsifier: A reversible model satisfying the stated FDT pairing and spectral assumptions but violating its spectral-resolvent sum would falsify the claim.
primary_prior_art: Kubo 1957 is the general response-correlation source; the spectral expansion here is a direct resolvent consequence under the explicit self-adjointness and overlap assumptions.
limits: Continuous spectral measures require the corresponding integral formulation.
Non-reversible systems may have non-normal resolvent growth not captured by eigenvalues alone.
